2026-08-26.headline: Edge gets Process Isolation and clipboard suggestion toggles on Windows, while Defender's 'Controlled Configuration' is now 'Configuration Protection (Preview)' and Linux settings shuffle into a new category.
highlights: Windows, Microsoft Edge: 8 new settings, including Process Isolation toggles (device and user) and clipboard suggestions in the address bar; Process Isolation is worth enabling for extra hardening.

Windows, Defender: the setting formerly known as 'Controlled Configuration' is now 'Configuration Protection (Preview)', but the option list still has 3 entries, so the rename is just a badge refresh.
Linux: a memory scan setting moved into the brand-new 'Advanced Settings' category while 'Advanced Protection' was retired; pure reorganization, no functional change.
2026-08-26.watchOut: The Defender rename and Linux category shuffle are cosmetic, profiles keep working since they reference setting IDs, not display names. No breakage.

2026-08-18.headline: macOS Content Cache gets a full control panel (38 new settings), Windows Update for Business adds maintenance window scheduling, and Web Content Filter arrives for iOS and macOS.
highlights: macOS: 38 new Content Cache settings, covering caching limits, peer listen ranges, tethered caching, and keep-awake behavior; a long-awaited expansion for Apple fleets.
Windows: 29 new Maintenance Window settings across Windows Update for Business and a dedicated Maintenance Windows category, with monthly and weekly schedules, start times, and durations.
iOS and macOS: Web Content Filter gains 12 settings including plugin configuration and filtering, plus a new DNS Proxy category with 4 settings for custom DNS setups.
Android Enterprise: new controls for eSIM removal on wipe, separate work lock requirement, and screen behavior; small but useful for compliance policies.
2026-08-18.watchOut: The picker got a major cleanup: 271 categories removed with zero setting removals, so no deployed profiles will break; it's just reorganization. Also, Add-on Management and Azure Virtual Desktop categories had changes, but no details on what shifted.

2026-08-06.headline: Slow day: one Linux setting got its internal identifier renamed, nothing else moved.
highlights: Linux: Platform Update Fixed Version setting's offsetUri changed from 'version' to 'fixedVersion'; metadata only, no functional impact.

2026-08-02.headline: Quiet day: Android catalog loses five settings, from eSIM wipe to work profile lock.
highlights: Android: General category drops 'Remove all eSIMs during a device wipe' and 'Maximum days to turn off work profile'.
Android: Misc settings lose screen timeout and screen-on-while-plugged controls.
Android: Work profile password removes the separate work lock requirement.
2026-08-02.watchOut: If any of your profiles use these settings, check for replacements; the catalog no longer lists them.

2026-08-01.headline: One new Windows security setting for Entra ID enforcement, plus a picker tidy-up; a quiet day in the catalog.
highlights: Windows: New Security setting 'Enable Microsoft Entra ID Authentication Enforcement' lets you require Entra ID authentication; worth a look if you're moving to passwordless.
Windows: 'Select Transport Type' under Connections had its option list refreshed, but the count stayed at 3; check if your chosen option still exists.
The 'Power' category was removed from the picker; existing profiles keep working since categories are just labels.

2026-07-30.headline: iOS and macOS get per-app permission controls (Location, Camera, Microphone) in the Settings Catalog, plus a pile of Android and Linux scheduling knobs.
highlights: iOS/macOS: 30 new App Settings and Safari Browser settings let you lock down per-app permissions like Location, Microphone, Camera, and Org Justification; macOS also gets allowed/denied binaries and accessibility controls

Windows: 10 new Edge settings include CPU performance tier override and strict MIME type checking for worker scripts; 9 Writing Assistance settings block specific apps/URLs and lock the first-run experience
Linux: Platform Update scheduling arrives with month, day-of-week, start/end times, and fixed version; Defender adds memory scan preview (requires Behavior Monitoring)
Android: New General settings to remove all eSIMs during a device wipe and cap how long a work profile can stay off; Power settings for screen timeout and screen-on-while-plugged
2026-07-30.watchOut: Two UAC settings (Admin Approval Mode and Elevation Prompt for Administrator Protection) changed applicability: minimum supported version jumped from 10.0.25272 to 10.0.26100.7019 (Windows 11 24H2) and the CSP version dropped from 11 to 6. Existing assignments to older Windows builds will stop applying.

2026-07-22.headline: OneDrive sync gains OIDC auth for on-prem SharePoint and hard-delete on unmount or permission loss, while a new Windows App category takes over Remote Desktop client management.
highlights: Windows: OneDrive adds OIDC authentication for on-prem SharePoint syncing, a 'prevent offline mode' control for shared libraries, and hard-deletion of folders when unmounted or when users lose access. Great for hybrid setups, just double-check your data-retention policy.
Windows: New 'Windows App' policy category manages the Remote Desktop client: turn off auto-updates, pick an Admin Release Ring, skip the first-run experience, and enforce inactivity logoff.
Windows: Browser content settings now allow or block the Local Fonts permission per site, a subtle privacy lever.
Windows: Win RE gains settings to enable Windows Recovery Environment and auto remediation, a nice option for self-healing devices.
2026-07-22.watchOut: No removals today; the only changes are two macOS account name descriptions now suggesting {{serialNumber}} for userless ADE devices, a recommendation rather than a requirement.

2026-07-17.headline: Windows finally gets per-app Store app removal (Teams, Photos, Copilot, the whole Xbox suite) plus a dynamic list for bulk debloat, while WSL containers gain a registry allowlist and Keyboard Filter picks up Insider settings.
highlights: Windows: 27 new App Package Deployment settings; per-app toggles for in-box Store apps plus 'Remove Microsoft Store apps with dynamic list' for a rolling purge. The debloat crowd has waited a decade for this.
Windows: 5 new Keyboard Filter settings (Insider preview) for blocked keys and scancodes, breakout key, and admin exemption; kiosk builders can now fine-tune input lockdown.
Windows: WSL containers get an allowlist for permitted registries; worth enforcing before someone pulls an image from somewhere imaginative.
Linux: Antivirus engine Enforcement Level gains an Audit option (logs detections without blocking) alongside Real-time, On-demand, and Passive modes; handy for validation.
2026-07-17.watchOut: No breakage: the 26 changed settings simply bump max supported Windows version to 26200, the added categories are picker reorganization, and the Linux Antivirus change adds an option without removing any.

2026-07-10.headline: Windows picks up 8 new Privilege Management settings for fine-tuning elevation rules (user applicability, validation, action types); a quiet day otherwise, unless you live for option-list refreshes.
highlights: Windows: 8 new Privilege Management settings, including user applicability, validation, and elevation action, give admins more granular control over when and how elevation happens.
Windows: One Connectivity setting (Disable Cross Device Resume) got its option list refreshed; count stayed the same, so don't expect any behavior change.

2026-07-01.headline: A quiet day in the catalog: Windows picks up a single new Camera setting, Configure Camera Options, so admins get one more lever for webcam policy.
highlights: Windows: New 'Configure Camera Options' setting under Camera, likely for managing camera privacy or behavior; only one new setting today, so don't expect fireworks

2026-07.headline: Windows gets per-app removal toggles for in-box Store apps plus a WSL container allowlist, the month's clear standout.
2026-07.overview: July's catalog refresh is dominated by Windows: per-app removal toggles for the in-box Store apps (Teams, Photos, Copilot, and the usual suspects) plus a dynamic-list option for a rolling purge. Apple picked up declarative app settings for iOS and macOS, and Linux gained platform update scheduling controls. Behind the scenes, 3,900+ settings were shuffled to a new category ID, which is pure picker reorganization. Nothing broke, but your filter muscle memory will need a refresh.

sections.body: July's Windows story is about finally being able to strip the in-box cruft. The App Package Deployment category gained 27 settings that let you remove specific Store apps (Microsoft Teams, Photos, Copilot, the Xbox suite) with per-app toggles, plus a dynamic-list option for a rolling purge. Security-wise, WSL containers got an allowlist for permitted registries, so you can stop people pulling from anywhere. Edge added a Copilot address bar suggestions toggle and some worker script restrictions. OneDrive gained OIDC auth for on-prem SharePoint syncing. Under the hood, 3,903 settings were moved to a new category ID; that's picker reorganization, not functional change, but if you've hardcoded category GUIDs in scripts, they're now pointing at a moving target.

Apple fans get a stack of new declarative app settings for iOS and macOS, covering per-app permissions like Camera, Microphone, and Location, with signing ID and team ID controls. Safari picked up similar privacy permission defaults. iOS and macOS also gained Siri and Intelligence toggles (Force Reduce Sensitive Content, Allow Natural Language Editing, and friends). A few older Privacy Preferences Policy Control settings (Camera, Accessibility, Bluetooth Always) are now marked deprecated, which is a heads-up that they'll be going away eventually.
Android is quiet: a couple of eSIM wipe behaviors, a work profile password requirement toggle, and some power settings. Worth a look if you've been asked to nuke roaming eSIMs on wipe.

Linux admins finally get platform update scheduling controls (day of month, week, window start/end, fixed version) under Platform Update, so you can gate when devices pick up updates. Defender also gained a memory scan preview and an extra Enforcement Level option.

2026-07.watchOut: The category reorganization means category IDs are not stable; if you've built automation on them, expect breakage. Also macOS privacy settings marked deprecated; plan to migrate to the new App Settings equivalents.

2026-06-25.headline: A light Edge day: new CPU performance overrides and local font permission controls, plus two Wallet features finally get the deprecation badge.
highlights: Windows, macOS: 4 new Edge policies for performance, including overriding the CPU performance tier and forcing foreground priority on specific URLs, plus a Copilot address bar suggestion toggle.
Windows, macOS: 3 new Content settings for Local Fonts permission; set a default and add site-level allow/block overrides to stop font fingerprinting.
Windows, macOS: Edge Wallet Donation and Edge Wallet E-Tree settings are now marked 'Deprecated' in the display name; start planning to remove them from profiles.
63 Edge policy descriptions got rewording across the board; purely cosmetic edits, no functional change.
2026-06-25.watchOut: One setting, 'Allows web pages to use identifiers for protected content playback', lost macOS from its applicability and is now Windows-only; any macOS profile using it will stop applying it after this change.

2026-06-24.headline: Android gains a Connectivity category with 11 radio and network lockdowns (2G, VPN, network reset, Wi-Fi minimums) plus eSIM blocking, and Windows Autopilot prep now takes 25 allowed apps instead of 10.
highlights: Android: 11 new Connectivity settings block 2G, cellular network resets, VPN configuration, SMS, airplane mode, and require a minimum Wi-Fi security level; General adds a block on eSIM profile installs, wallpaper, and user icon changes.

Windows: Autopilot device preparation now supports up to 25 allowed apps (was 10) and reports install status to the preparation deployment report; the script description now says 'Windows PowerShell' and points to the same report.
tvOS and visionOS: Setup Assistant gains controls for Screen Saver, TV Provider Sign In, TV Room, TV Home Screen Sync, and Tips.
Windows: One new User Rights setting, Adjust Memory Quotas For Process, joins the catalog.
2026-06-24.watchOut: 39 Windows App Package Deployment settings (like removing default Store apps) now have a maximum supported version of 10.0.26100.8116; on newer Windows builds those settings will no longer apply, so check your profiles. Three Out-of-box experience settings also had their option lists changed, but the specifics aren't shown.

2026-06-10.headline: Edge on Windows and macOS gains Copilot URL controls and developer tools restrictions; a New Tab Page feed switch joins in, while 111 settings get description rewrites.
highlights: Windows and macOS: New 'Browsing with Copilot' policies let you allow or block specific URLs, and toggle automatic opening of the Copilot side pane from Outlook links.
Windows and macOS: Developer tools can now be restricted via allow and block URL patterns, giving you finer control over where the F12 console works.
Windows and macOS: The New Tab Page gains a default feed tab setting (Work or Discover), with a separate user-override variant.
2026-06-10.watchOut: No breaking changes; 111 settings got description rewordings only. For the new Copilot and New Tab Page policies, note the 'users can override' variants exist, so choose the non-override ones for strict enforcement.

2026-06.headline: Android Enterprise connectivity lockdown leads June's catalog, with Edge Copilot controls close behind.
2026-06.overview: Three update days brought a new Connectivity category for Android Enterprise, a wave of Edge Copilot policies for Windows and macOS, and a few Setup Assistant extras for Apple platforms. No settings were removed, but 176 Edge descriptions were rewritten and Windows app package applicability got a version bump.

sections.body: The Edge Copilot additions are the main event: address bar suggestions, new tab page configuration, allowed/blocked URLs for browsing with Copilot, and an auto-open side pane for Outlook links. Also new is a User Rights setting for Adjust Memory Quotas For Process and Local Fonts permission controls in Content settings. The 176 description rewrites are cosmetic, but Wallet Donation and Edge Wallet E-Tree got the Deprecated stamp, so start planning to retire those. App Package Deployment settings now support an OS max of 10.0.26100.8116; recheck any version filters.

macOS inherits the same Edge Copilot and Local Fonts policies as Windows. For iOS/tvOS, there's a new Tap to Setup option; tvOS adds Screen Saver, TV Provider Sign In, TV Room, and TV Home Screen Sync to Setup Assistant; visionOS picks up Tips. Also new is a macOS/Windows setting to allow M365 authentication popups in work profiles.

The Connectivity category is the headline: block outgoing calls, airplane mode, cellular 2G, SMS, network reset, mobile network config, VPN config, cell broadcasts, and ultra wideband, plus a minimum Wi-Fi security level. General blocks eSIM profile adds, wallpaper and user icon changes, and printing; Applications blocks widgets and app functions from work profile apps. This gives you real control over device radios and connectivity, which is a solid security win.

2026-06.watchOut: The Windows App Package Deployment applicability bump to 10.0.26100.8116 means OS-version filters need a refresh. Edge Wallet Donation and E-Tree policies are now marked deprecated, so expect them to fade; migrate away.

2026-05-27.headline: Edge picks up a batch of Copilot and New Tab Page controls, macOS adds local account management, and iOS restriction settings start getting deprecation tags.
highlights: Windows: 28 new Edge settings for Copilot, including allowed/blocked URLs for browsing with Copilot, the Copilot new tab page, and blocking developer tools by URL pattern; plus 12 more New Tab Page feed settings.
macOS: New 'Account settings' category with 10 settings for local admin and primary account creation, password rotation, and prefilled info, plus Setup Assistant additions for FileVault and iCloud.
iOS: Setup Assistant gained a few toggles (camera button, safety and handling, etc.), and several restriction settings got '(Deprecated)' in their names, signaling future removal.
Windows: Agent Governance settings got clearer descriptions and an extra option for 'Agent user account', worth a review before they affect existing policies.
2026-05-27.watchOut: The iOS deprecation renames are a heads-up to plan for those toggles disappearing; also the Agent Governance description changes might shift how you interpret current policies.

2026-05-21.headline: Windows adds Agent Governance, nine settings to decide exactly which files, networks, and tools your agents can touch.
highlights: Windows: New Agent Governance category; settings control allowed filesystem directories, network access, tool execution, and agent user identity
Windows: Access level and targeted agent settings let you scope down what an agent can do per workload
2026-05-21.watchOut: The lone removal: 'Specify additional package family names to remove' from App Package Deployment; if you had that configured, it's gone from the catalog and will need a rethink.

2026-05.headline: May: Windows gets Agent Governance for AI agents and a boatload of Edge Copilot URL controls, while Apple deprecates a long list of Apple Intelligence restrictions.
2026-05.overview: Two update days this month, and most of the action is Windows: a new Agent Governance category for locking down what AI agents can touch on disk and network, plus dozens of Edge policies for Copilot browsing patterns and new tab page feeds. Apple deprecated a wall of Assistant and Intelligence settings (they're renamed, not gone), and macOS gained local account creation with password rotation. Android picked up a single Bluetooth sharing block.

sections.body: The big new thing is Agent Governance, a whole category for sandboxing AI agents: allowed filesystem directories (deny by default), network access toggles, execution in container, and a new 'agent user account' option. Edge also got a Copilot takeover: URL allow and block lists for browsing-with-Copilot, a side pane auto-open for Outlook links, and a setting to block developer tools by URL pattern. On the debloat side, the 'additional package family names to remove' setting got pulled, so the in-box app removal picker is now your only lever. Microsoft also added OLE Graph and OrgChart blocking and a couple of MAM enrollment toggles.

macOS picked up Account settings for creating a local primary or admin account with password rotation (yes, rotation) and prefill options, plus new Setup Assistant panes to skip (FileVault, iCloud Storage, Accessibility, and the like). iOS added a few Setup Assistant skips too (Safety and handling, Web Content Filtering, Multitasking, Camera button). And if you use Restrictions, a bunch of Assistant, Dictation, and Apple Intelligence settings got renamed with a '(Deprecated)' suffix. They still work, but if you're building new profiles, you might want to plan for the alternative settings.
One new setting: block Bluetooth sharing on Android Enterprise devices. That's it.

2026-05.watchOut: The removed package family names setting means if you were using it to strip out extra apps, that approach is gone; the per-app removal list is still there. Also, the Apple deprecation renames could break your reporting or naming conventions, but the settings themselves still function.

2026-04-30.headline: Edge for macOS gets a 67-setting dump including Scareware blocker and local-network request controls, while Linux antivirus gains scheduled scans and offline definition updates.
highlights: macOS: 67 new Microsoft Edge settings; the useful ones include Scareware blocker, TLS 1.3 Early Data control, per-site geolocation and full-screen blocking, and a privacy-friendly 'Reduce IP Address Change Notification' toggle.
Linux: 10 Schedule Scan settings (daily/weekly, idle and low-priority runs, randomization) plus 6 Antivirus engine options for offline definition updates with cloud fallback.

Windows: Device Lock picks up password policy settings (min length, max age, complexity, history) and an admin lockout option; App Package Deployment adds a way to specify extra package family names to remove.
Windows: Edge also gains 14 settings, including guest mode enforcement and InPrivate URL allow/block lists.
2026-04-30.watchOut: A few Edge security settings are marked obsolete (e.g., 'Enhance the security state'), and network request settings were renamed to cover 'local devices' as well as endpoints. Also, the minimum supported version for 'Disable Cross Device Resume' jumped to 10.0.26100.7705, so older Windows builds won't see that policy.

2026-04.headline: Edge dominates April with over 80 new settings, and Linux Defender finally gets scheduled scan controls.
2026-04.overview: One update day, and it was mostly about Edge: new policies for AI, TLS, and scareware blocking across macOS and Windows. Linux security admins get long-requested scheduled scan and offline definition update options. Everything else is housekeeping: a few renames, one option list growth, and a compatibility bump that could affect existing assignments.

sections.body: Windows picks up 14 new Edge settings including InPrivate URL allow/block lists, guest mode enforcement, and foreground tab priority. The network request policies were renamed to clarify they cover local devices and local network endpoints separately, and a new Device Lock category adds password policies (length, age, complexity, history). OOBE gains two toggles: hide change account options and install Windows updates during setup. Also note that Cross Device Resume dropped its Insider-only tag and now requires Windows 11 24H2 or newer.

macOS gets the bulk of the Edge action: 67 new settings ranging from TLS 1.3 Early Data and built-in AI APIs to a configurable scareware blocker that can share suspicious URLs with Defender SmartScreen. iOS sees one addition, Enable Registration During Setup for Extensible SSO, which could simplify deployment of SSO extensions during device enrollment.

Android has almost nothing this month: the Location setting in General was renamed from Block location to Location, and its options grew from two to three. Presumably that means you can now choose an allow state, but that's about it.

Defender for Endpoint on Linux gains scheduled scan controls: daily or weekly scans, idle and low CPU options, and a toggle to ignore exclusions. There's also offline definition update configuration with a fallback to cloud, plus a settable security intelligence update interval. This gives admin much needed flexibility for when scans run and how definitions get refreshed on Linux fleets.

2026-04.watchOut: The Cross Device Resume setting now requires Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100) or later; if you previously assigned it to older builds, it will stop applying. Also, several Edge security state policies are now marked obsolete, so expect them to be removed eventually and plan your migration.

2026-03-26.headline: Windows gets new browser controls to keep shady sites out of your local network, and Apple Intelligence finally has a settings category you can boss around.
highlights: Windows: 22 new Network settings to block or allow site requests to local network endpoints and the local device, plus IP address space overrides; a handy way to stop internal network snooping.
iOS/macOS: 15 new Apple Intelligence settings covering Smart Replies, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, and forced on-device processing for Dictation and Translation.
macOS: Tamper protection policies now also cover Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, so the sensor itself is guarded.
Windows: 8 new Cryptography compliance policies let you prefer specific TLS cipher and key exchange algorithms for hardening.
2026-03-26.watchOut: A bunch of Microsoft Edge policies got marked deprecated in the rename; no replacements listed yet, so if you're using any, it's worth checking before they get pulled.

2026-03-03.headline: Quiet day at the catalog: zero settings added, removed, or changed, just some category reshuffling that won't touch your policies.
highlights: No new or deprecated settings across any platform, so the picker is frozen solid today.
3 categories appeared (Custom, When sending a message, Microsoft One Note 2016) and 10 others got reorganized; that's picker housekeeping, not policy impact.

2026-03-02.headline: A quiet Monday: no new or removed settings, just a few category renames and additions in the Settings Catalog picker. Nothing that should change your configuration game.
highlights: Three new categories appear in the picker (Custom, When sending a message, Microsoft One Note 2016), likely from an app provider's template, but no actual settings were added with them.

Ten existing categories got metadata updates (including ones named 'Deprecated policies' and 'Removed policies'), which sounds ominous but is just picker reorganization; your deployed profiles reference settings, not categories.

2026-03-01.headline: Windows picks up policy control for Edge HTTPS-Only Mode and a set of Office macro security guardrails, alongside idle detection and kiosk lockdown toggles.
highlights: Windows: New Edge policies for HTTPS-Only Mode (both user and device scope) let admins control whether users can enable the feature, a solid win for enforcing secure browsing.
Windows: Office macro security gets tougher with options to block all internet macros, require signed macros, and turn off Trusted Documents for VBA, closing some classic attack paths.
Windows: Idle detection controls appear, allowing per-site or global allow/block rules, handy for keeping kiosks awake or preventing sleep on specific sites.
Windows: Custom settings for disabling specific shortcut keys and command bar IDs show up, useful for locking down Office apps in shared or kiosk scenarios.
2026-03-01.watchOut: No removals or changed settings; the 10 category edits are just picker reorganization, so existing profiles are unaffected.

2026-03.headline: Windows gets private network access guardrails while Apple Intelligence becomes a managed setting; also a pile of Edge policies got blessed with the 'Deprecated' sticker.
2026-03.overview: Four update days in March, and the catalog grew in both volume and intent. Windows picked up a solid set of network security controls for browser access to local endpoints, and Apple finally exposed Apple Intelligence features as configurable policy settings. Many Edge settings got description rewrites and deprecation flags; nothing broke, but your policy filtering might need a look.

sections.body: The big one is a cluster of 22 Network settings that let you block or allow sites from making requests to local network endpoints and the local device. That's the Private Network Access story, and it's a security win if you want to keep rogue websites from poking at your intranet. Also new: 8 Cryptography compliance policies to pin down TLS cipher and key exchange algorithms, which is nice if you're tired of negotiating. Edge got a few new toggles, including HTTPS-Only Mode enforcement and storage quota controls, but more visibly, dozens of its policies got their display names suffixed with '(Deprecated)' and descriptions rewritten from 'will' to 'is' - Microsoft's copyediting budget clearly went somewhere. Windows AI picked up a 'Remove Microsoft Copilot App' setting, because sometimes you just want it gone. Remote Remediation settings now apply to two new SKUs (iotEnterpriseSEval and windowsCPC), so if you were excluding those, you might want to reconsider.

Apple's month is all about the AI. A new Intelligence Settings category brings 15 settings across macOS and iOS to control Apple Intelligence features: Smart Replies, Writing Tools, Image Playground, Genmoji, on-device dictation, and more. Also new: External Intelligence Settings for managing sign-in and allowed workspace IDs, plus Siri Settings with a profanity filter toggle (because someone asked). Keyboard settings landed for iOS and macOS, and File Provider gained controls for external volume syncing. On the security side, macOS Tamper Protection and Antivirus engine settings now also work via microsoftSense, meaning Defender for Endpoint can manage them, and a batch of enrollment settings now target macOS in addition to iOS - so check if you have profiles that should stay iOS-only.

2026-03.watchOut: Several categories and settings were renamed with deprecated markers; if you have profiles referencing the old display names, they still map, but you'll see 'Deprecated' in the UI. Also, the enrollment settings that now include macOS could widen your scope unexpectedly if you had them scoped to iOS.

2026-02-25.headline: macOS antivirus engine gains offline security intelligence updates, letting you serve definitions from a mirror URL for air-gapped or restricted networks.
highlights: macOS: new Antivirus engine settings for offline definition updates: set a mirror URL, enable offline updates, and verify signature on the offline packages via a Features setting.
iOS/macOS: Apple is renaming 'Rapid Security Responses' to 'Background Security Improvements' in Software Update settings; update any policies or comms that reference the old term.
iOS/macOS: Force Delayed Software Updates, the Software Update Settings category, and AirPlay Device ID are now flagged as deprecated; expect them to be removed in a future release.
Windows: Remote Remediation settings (all Windows Insiders only) got cleaner descriptions and lost the '[Pending fix]' tags from display names, but no functional change.
2026-02-25.watchOut: If you use the deprecated iOS/macOS settings (Force Delayed Software Updates, Software Update Settings, AirPlay Device ID), start planning replacements. Also, the Rapid Security Responses rename means you may need to adjust existing Software Update policies to keep them aligned.

2026-02.headline: February was a quiet one: macOS gains offline antivirus intelligence, Apple renames Rapid Security Responses to Background Security Improvements.
2026-02.overview: One update day this month, and it was mostly housekeeping. macOS picked up offline security intelligence settings for the Antivirus engine, Apple rebranded Rapid Security Responses as Background Security Improvements, and a handful of older settings got marked deprecated. Windows saw only description cleanups and a pending-fix label removal.

sections.body: Windows didn't gain any new settings this month. The changes are limited to reworded descriptions for the Windows Insiders-only Remote Remediation settings, clarifying that retry interval and time-to-reboot only take effect when auto remediation is on, plus a few display name fixes that dropped a '[Pending fix]' suffix. If you're not on Insider builds, this month was a no-op.

macOS gets the interesting stuff: three new Antivirus engine settings for offline security intelligence updates, including a mirror server URL and signature verification. On both iOS and macOS, Apple renamed 'Rapid Security Responses' to 'Background Security Improvements' across the Software Update Settings, so update your documentation. Also flagged as deprecated: Force Delayed Software Updates, the iOS Software Update Settings, and AirPlay Device ID, so expect those to be removed in a future release.

2026-02.watchOut: Apple's rename of Rapid Security Responses to Background Security Improvements could trip up any scripts or policies that reference the old name. Also, the deprecations mean those settings should be replaced before they're pulled.
